name: Kerala
title: Holidays in Kerala
intro: Houseboats on palm-lined backwaters, tea hills and spice markets in southern India. Here's what Kerala is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 4½ to 5½ hrs ahead of the UK

facts_note: Ask your GP or a travel clinic about jabs before you go. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: December to February is the best time, warm and dry with green countryside. March and April get very hot and humid. The south-west monsoon brings heavy rain from June to September, and more rain falls in October and November. The hills around Munnar stay cooler all year.

things.name: Backwater houseboat
things.blurb: Spend a night on a kettuvallam rice boat near Alleppey, watching village life drift by.

things.name: Fort Kochi
things.blurb: Walk past Chinese fishing nets, old churches and spice warehouses in the historic port.

things.name: Kathakali show
things.blurb: A colourful dance-drama with elaborate make-up. Arrive early to watch the performers get ready.

things.name: Munnar tea estates
things.blurb: Cool hills covered in tea bushes, with a tea museum and easy walks.

things.name: Periyar Tiger Reserve
things.blurb: Boat trips and guided walks in Thekkady to spot elephants, bison and birds.

things.name: Varkala
things.blurb: A clifftop town above a sandy beach, good for a few days of rest at the end of a trip.

faqs.question: Is Kerala good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is one of the gentlest introductions to India, with calm backwaters, cooler hills and beaches. Food can be mild or spicy, and hotels are used to cooking for children.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Ten to fourteen nights. A classic route is Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady, a night on a houseboat, then a beach to finish.

faqs.question: How do you get there from the UK?
faqs.answer: Most families fly to Kochi via the Gulf, changing in Dubai, Doha or Abu Dhabi. British passport holders need an Indian eVisa, applied for online before travel.

faqs.question: How do you get around?
faqs.answer: Most families hire a car and driver for the trip, which is good value and avoids driving on busy roads. Trains are an option for longer hops.
